thesis: Dell raised full-year FY2027 revenue guidance to $192.0B and EPS to $24.37 after a record Q2 FY2027 print (Sept 2, 2026): revenue $47B (+58% YoY), EPS $6.34 (+273% YoY), a record $60.9B in AI server orders, and a record $95B AI-server backlog — a specific, already-confirmed, company-disclosed event, not a forward promise. The clearest counter-case is valuation/execution risk on converting that backlog to shipped revenue, but Dell already demonstrated conversion this quarter (record revenue, not just bookings), which is why analysts including Evercore ISI ($550 target) and Loop Capital ($600 target) raised price targets rather than flagging backlog risk. Kept at low conviction purely on the governance flag below, not on the strength of the catalyst itself.
invalidation: AI server bookings-to-revenue conversion stalls in Q3 FY2027 guidance/print, or the full-year guidance raise is walked back.

thesis: SK hynix's Q2 2026 results (revenue +257% YoY, operating income $42B, +557% YoY) and HBM4 mass-shipment ramp are a specific, already-confirmed, company-disclosed catalyst behind the 60-day price move, reinforced by a Sept 9 JPMorgan Overweight initiation. The counter-case is a pending DRAM price-fixing class action (Samsung/SK Hynix/Micron, N.D. Cal.) plus a Korean breach-of-trust investigation naming three executives as subjects (not yet defendants) — real overhangs, but neither has a scheduled ruling, hearing, or trial date disclosed, and memory chip stocks broadly wobbled pre-market Sept 10 on macro sentiment rather than company-specific news, which keeps this from a clean high-conviction read.
invalidation: HBM demand growth stalls, capex guidance is cut, or a court/prosecutor sets a near-term hearing or trial date on the DRAM price-fixing suit or the executive breach-of-trust investigation.

thesis: Navan's Q2 FY2027 results (released after close Sept 9) beat expectations, yet the stock fell ~22% Thursday (Sept 10) as investors focused on decelerating usage yield and a broader AI-valuation-driven de-risking across growth names rather than a company-specific fundamental miss. That beat-but-crashed, macro/sector-tinted reaction is a mixed signal rather than a resolved directional read either way. A securities class action over the October 2025 IPO's registration-statement disclosures (sales-and-marketing expense growth, CFO departure) remains pending but has no scheduled hearing or trial date within the next ~90 days, so it doesn't rise to a risk_flags-level concern for a direction that isn't being taken long anyway.
invalidation: Stock stabilizes and usage-yield/margin trends inflect positively over the next 1-2 quarters, or the litigation overhang resolves without material liability.

thesis: Vertiv missed Q2 2026 revenue estimates ($3.27B vs. $3.38B consensus, reported July 29) on what management called 'minor timing shifts' in AI data-center project conversion, and the stock is down roughly 32% from its 52-week high, with a Hagens Berman securities-law investigation opened in August over whether execution risks were adequately disclosed — a specific, already-confirmed, company-disclosed catalyst (the earnings miss itself), not a rumor. The counter-case — that this is genuine AI data-center demand destruction rather than timing — is undercut by Vertiv's subsequent $1.45B Utility Innovation Group acquisition to expand power-constrained data-center capacity and a broadly bullish 28-analyst consensus (24 buy-or-better, 4 hold, 0 sell, Loop Capital $500 target). No risk_flags criterion is met: the Hagens Berman probe and the pending Delaware derivative suit are open investigations/allegations with no confirmed finding and no scheduled hearing or trial date.
invalidation: Q3 2026 results repeat the revenue miss, or clear evidence emerges that AI data-center order-to-revenue conversion is structurally slowing rather than a timing issue.

thesis: No Step-2 signal threshold triggered this cycle (60-day price move +9.9%, volume in line with average, 7.7% off the 52-week high) but as a held position NVDA gets a fresh thesis regardless. The company confirmed a $12.9B acquisition of Hugging Face to scale LLM serving, and the stock sits within striking distance of its May 2026 record high. Ongoing DOJ/Congressional scrutiny of the Groq licensing structure and a French antitrust probe are real but open-ended, with no confirmed finding and no scheduled ruling or hearing date, so risk_flags stays empty. Kept at medium rather than high since the picture rests on several contributing factors (M&A, steady demand, multiple pending-but-undated regulatory inquiries) without one dominant, cleanly-resolved catalyst.
invalidation: DOJ, FTC, or French antitrust action escalates to formal charges or a specific near-term hearing/ruling date, or the Hugging Face integration fails to advance the stated AI-platform strategy.

thesis: AXT posted record Q2 2026 revenue of $47.6M on indium phosphide substrate demand and signed a multi-year supply agreement with Lumentum (deposits through 2031, first $43.5M due within 30 business days of the July signing) — a specific, already-confirmed, company-disclosed catalyst behind the 60-day price move. The clearest counter-case is stretched valuation (~21x annualized sales on a ~$4B market cap) and single-day volatility partly attributed to leveraged-ETF flows rather than pure fundamentals; that mechanical/momentum component is real enough to keep this at medium rather than high, though it doesn't erase the underlying signed-contract catalyst. A 2024 short-seller-driven investigation (J Capital Research allegations) surfaced no confirmed finding and has no scheduled next step, so per the fixed rubric it doesn't qualify as a governance_history or active_litigation flag.
invalidation: Lumentum agreement volumes or deposit schedule fall short of disclosed terms, or revenue growth reverses without the signed-contract backdrop holding.
